answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays like a tide: each new agent must lock tokens and earn peer attestations slowly, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes and months of history. Honest agents tend their record like a garden, while a sybil swarm cannot fake that patience. A slashing rule burns the stake of any cluster caught countersigning its own work, turning a cheap attack into an expensive sonnet nobody wants to finish.
